questions.q: Why didn't Jim ride straight to Dr. Livesey as the captain had told him?
choices: It would have left his mother alone and unprotected
He did not know how to ride a horse
The road was blocked by snow
questions.evidence: would have left my mother alone and unprotected

questions.q: Where did Jim and his mother first go for help?
questions.evidence: seek help in the neighbouring hamlet

questions.q: How did the people of the hamlet respond when asked to come back to the inn?
choices: No one would agree to return with them
All the men grabbed weapons and came along
They laughed and said the danger was imaginary
They sent for soldiers from the town
questions.evidence: no soul would consent to return with us to the Admiral Benbow

questions.q: Why were the people of the hamlet so afraid?
choices: The name of Captain Flint filled them with terror
They thought the inn was haunted
They owed money to the captain
questions.evidence: The name of Captain Flint, though it was strange to me, was well enough known to some there and carried a great weight of terror.

questions.q: What does Jim's mother's speech to the neighbours show about her?
choices: She was brave and determined to get what was owed to her son
She was eager to give up and leave the area
She wanted the neighbours to keep the gold
She was more frightened than anyone
questions.evidence: If none of the rest of you dare," she said, "Jim and I dare.

questions.q: The neighbours cried out at Jim and his mother's "foolhardiness." What does "foolhardiness" mean?
questions.evidence: they all cried out at our foolhardiness

questions.q: What did the neighbours give Jim before he went back to the inn?
questions.evidence: give me a loaded pistol lest we were attacked

questions.q: What message was written on the back of the black spot?
Where did Jim finally find the key to the sea-chest?
choices: On a string around the captain's neck
questions.evidence: hanging to a bit of tarry string

questions.q: What letter was burned on the top of the sea-chest?
questions.evidence: the initial "B" burned on the top of it

questions.q: What were the last two things at the bottom of the chest?
choices: A bundle in oilcloth and a canvas bag of gold
questions.evidence: a bundle tied up in oilcloth, and looking like papers, and a canvas bag that gave forth, at a touch, the jingle of gold

questions.q: How much money did Jim's mother insist on taking from the captain's bag?
choices: Exactly what was owed, and not a farthing more
questions.evidence: I'll have my dues, and not a farthing over.

questions.q: Why was counting the money so slow and difficult?
choices: The coins were from many countries, and she could count only in guineas
Jim's mother could not read numbers
The bag had a hole in it
questions.evidence: the coins were of all countries and sizes

questions.q: What sound made Jim stop his mother while she was counting the coins?
choices: The tap-tapping of the blind man's stick
questions.evidence: the tap-tapping of the blind man's stick upon the frozen road

questions.q: What finally made Jim's mother stop arguing and leave with the money she had counted?
choices: A low whistle from the hill
Dr. Livesey knocking at the door
questions.evidence: a little low whistle sounded a good way off upon the hill

questions.q: Where did Jim and his mother end up hiding at the end of the chapter?
choices: In a hedge by the inn
questions.evidence: drag her down the bank and a little way under the arch
